## Rule

ARC-GEN `868de0fa`: inputs are square grids (10..20) containing non-overlapping hollow blue square outlines, side lengths 3..10. Output preserves the blue outlines and fills each square interior orange (7) for odd side length, red (2) for even side length.

## Algorithm sketch

Fused-bank Path A (`build_task204_v1.py`): crop channel 1 and channel 0 to 20x20, cast blue to UINT8, run one 8-output `QLinearConv` with the shipped ring kernels for lengths 3..10, compare to ring thresholds, cast matches to UINT8, run one 2-output fill `QLinearConv`, then collapse background/blue/red/orange into a single UINT8 label-code canvas and broadcast `Equal(label, code_table)` as the BOOL output.

Task-shaped lower-cost Path B (`build_task204_v2.py`): use a sparse signed top-edge `QLinearConv` to detect each valid square top-left/length directly on the 18x18 possible top-left domain, then one 10x10 paint `QLinearConv` redraws the blue border plus red/orange fill codes. The valid square mask is recovered from the first row via `QLinearMatMul`; zero is reserved for padding before the final label-code `Equal`.

## Cost analysis

- 2026-06-30 (Claude re-audit): **Zero-sum theorem.** Scorer cost = `sum(intermediate bytes, dtype-aware)` + `sum(initializer elements, dtype-blind)`; `input`/`output` tensors are free. For an all-U8 pipeline, 1 intermediate byte ≡ 1 param element ≡ 1 cost unit, so moving work between conv-weights (params) and conv-outputs (memory) is exactly zero-sum, and adding any intermediate plane is strictly additive. The only sub-floor levers are (a) deleting a load-bearing tensor or (b) shrinking the two forced F32 input slices — both shown impossible. This is why every structural reshuffle (split, value-code, parity-decouple) lands at or above 7682.
- (superseded cost breakdowns for booltail/v1 → `_archive/task204_history.md`)
- 2026-05-31 v2: memory 6652 + params 1030. Largest tensors are the top-left detector `[1,8,18,18] UINT8 = 2592`, the detector input slice `[1,1,18,20] F32 = 1440`, and label pad `[1,1,30,30] UINT8 = 900`. Redrawing blue borders from anchors removes the full 20x20 blue slice; deriving the square valid mask from the first row removes the full 20x20 background slice. Remaining 400-byte planes are the paint canvas, `QLinearMatMul` background mask, and final label-code `Max`.

### Alternatives proved more expensive (2026-06-24):

- **Constant nodes for Slice/Pad index tensors**: tested; Constant outputs appear in `value_info` (memory), adding 192B vs initializers that only count as params elements. Probe: memory=6844 vs 6652.
- **Pad-before-Equal order (Equal then Pad)**: [1,10,20,20] BOOL intermediate = 2000B vs [1,1,30,30] U8 label = 900B. Current order is optimal.
- **Two-color crossing-parity (technique #50)**: crossing parity detects interior/exterior but not WHICH square size a cell belongs to. Separating odd-size and even-size crossings requires separate H_odd/H_even detection layers, which is more expensive than the current 8-channel detector.
- **Parity-only 2-channel detector**: cannot paint exact size-specific square patterns without knowing actual size L; all grouping schemes re-introduce 8 channels or add more expensive intermediates.
- **Smaller paint kernel**: max square = 10x10, so [1,8,10,10] = 800 elements is the minimum.
- **Narrower detector kernel [8,1,2,K<12]**: K=12 needed for max run length 10 + 2 guards (left/right). Cannot reduce.
- **Shared Slice start/end**: already shared (ch0_starts reused for both ch0 and ch1 row slices).
- **Run-length parity, weighted cumsum, spatial parity tricks**: all require larger intermediates or extra nodes to recover per-cell square size.

**Conclusion**: Task204 v2 (cost 7682) is at the algorithmic floor for this class of two-color hollow-square fill tasks with variable sizes 3..10.

## Don't-do log

_Record ruled-out hypotheses here so future agents don't retry them._

- Do NOT treat this as a "shape-only rearrange/crop" task (the ShapeOnlyRearrange card premise): FALSIFIED 2026-07-12. Fill colors red(2)/orange(7) are absent from every input (`in_colors=[0,1]`); the red-vs-orange choice is the enclosing square's side-length parity, a computed reduction, NOT a copyable/rearrangeable value. A static-index Slice/Gather/Pad/Concat graph cannot select it per-cell. floor_est ~1500 is fantasy (prices an impossible copy). Exact floor is the v2 template-match = 7682. See `hard_records/shape_only_rearrange_premise_falsified_2026-07-12.md`.
- Do NOT replace Slice/Pad index initializers with Constant nodes: constant outputs appear in `value_info` (memory), not params. Probe measured +192B memory overhead (6844 vs 6652). Initializers are cheaper.
- Do NOT try `sparse_initializer` to shave params on mostly-zero weights (paint_w nnz=380 vs 800; topleft_w nnz=76 vs 192). The official `sanitize_model` renames `graph.initializer` + node I/O but **never iterates `graph.sparse_initializer`** — the node input gets a `safe_name_N` while the sparse tensor keeps its old name → dangling ref → ORT fails to load → `score_network_v2` returns None. Empirically tested 2026-06-30. (Transferable to ALL tasks — see `.update/`.)
- Do NOT try a split/bucketed detector (separate convs per length-bucket): the param savings from right-sized paint kernels are exactly cancelled by the extra U8 merge/paint planes (zero-sum, 1 byte ≡ 1 param elem). Cropping large-L channels also requires illegal negative conv pads or an extra Slice. Net ≥ 0.
- Do NOT try Axes-shortened Slice index arrays: ch1_det and ch0_row each have 3 of 4 dims non-trivial, so an `axes` array makes the index initializers LONGER (9 vs 8 elems), not shorter.
- Do NOT try Equal-then-Pad ordering: [1,10,20,20] BOOL intermediate = 2000B vs [1,1,30,30] U8 label = 900B. Current Pad-then-Equal order is optimal.
- Do NOT attempt crossing-parity (technique #50) for two-color fill: technique #50 yields binary interior/exterior, not per-square size parity. Two separate H_odd/H_even detector passes require more intermediates than current 8-channel detector.
- Do NOT try to reduce to fewer than 8 top-left detector channels: 8 distinct square sizes (3..10) require 8 channels for both detection and painting.
- Do NOT try a 1-channel value-coded detector (encode length as UINT8 value): QLinearConv paint sums contributions from all positions in the receptive field; a single-channel value detector cannot be painted correctly when multiple squares are present.
- Do NOT rebuild as crossing-parity interior (#50) + vertical-span-parity color (nearest-blue-below−above via causal MaxPool + F16 tril-MatMul prefix-sum): BUILT + gated 2026-07-10 (`build_task204_v3_crossparity_span.py`). CORRECT (500/500 fresh ARC-GEN, visible 268/268) but profile=**18636** (2.43× floor). The size axis becomes 8×[1,1,20,20] F16 scan planes (6400 B, 2 B/elem) vs v2's single [1,8,18,18] U8 detector (2592 B, 1 B/elem); even fully fused it stays ~11k. The template-match packs the size axis into one 1-byte-per-elem tensor — strictly cheaper than any prefix/scan realization.
